sets.title: Standard English · 40 habits to unlearn
sets.instruction: Each sentence contains something common in everyday Singapore speech but marked wrong in a written exam. Choose the standard written form.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Can help me carry this or not?*
options: Could you help me carry this?
Can or not you help me?
You can help me carry this or not?
questions.m: Could you help me carry this?
a: Could you help me carry this?
questions.tip: A request in writing needs a subject and a question form.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Last time I very scared of dogs.*
options: I used to be very frightened of dogs.
Last time I very scared of dogs.
Last time I am very scared of dogs.
I last time was scared of dogs.
questions.m: I used to be very frightened of dogs.
a: I used to be very frightened of dogs.
questions.tip: 'Last time' meaning 'formerly' becomes 'used to'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *He got go to the camp.*
options: He got go to the camp.
He got to go the camp.
He has go to the camp.
questions.tip: 'Got' is not used to mark the past tense in written English.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Please on the fan.*
questions.tip: 'On' and 'off' are not verbs in written English; use 'switch on' or 'turn on'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *I will revert to you tomorrow.*
options: I will reply to you tomorrow.
I will revert to you tomorrow.
questions.m: I will reply to you tomorrow.
a: I will reply to you tomorrow.
questions.tip: 'Revert' means to go back to an earlier state, not to reply.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *The two sisters look same same.*
options: The two sisters look same same.
The two sisters look the same same.
The two sisters are look alike.
questions.tip: Repetition for emphasis is spoken usage only.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *I go and see the doctor already.*
options: I have already seen the doctor.
I go and see the doctor already.
I already go see the doctor.
I have already went to the doctor.
questions.m: I have already seen the doctor.
a: I have already seen the doctor.
questions.tip: 'Already' with a finished action takes the present perfect.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Where got so cheap one?*
questions.tip: 'Where got' expressing disbelief has no written equivalent; state the meaning plainly.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *My handphone spoil already.*
options: My mobile phone has stopped working.
questions.m: My mobile phone has stopped working.
a: My mobile phone has stopped working.
questions.tip: 'Spoil' for a device becomes 'break' or 'stop working'; 'handphone' is 'mobile phone' in formal writing.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Can you off the light?*
options: Could you switch off the light?
Can you off up the light?
questions.m: Could you switch off the light?
a: Could you switch off the light?
questions.tip: Use 'switch off' or 'turn off'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *I never go school yesterday.*
options: I did not go to school yesterday.
I not go to school yesterday.
questions.m: I did not go to school yesterday.
a: I did not go to school yesterday.
questions.tip: 'Never' means 'not once ever'; for a single day use 'did not'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *She is more taller than me.*
options: She is taller than I am.
She is more taller than me.
She is more tall than me.
She is taller than me is.
questions.m: She is taller than I am.
a: She is taller than I am.
questions.tip: Never use 'more' with an -er comparative.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *The food very nice.*
options: The food it is very nice.
questions.tip: Written English needs the verb 'to be'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Aiyah, so troublesome lah.*
questions.tip: Particles such as 'lah' and 'leh' do not appear in written English.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *I stay in Yishun.*
questions.tip: 'Stay' means a temporary visit; where you live permanently is 'live'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Kindly take note the deadline.*
options: Please kindly take note the deadline.
questions.tip: 'Take note' needs 'of'; the standard written form is simply 'Please note'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *He is one of my friend.*
options: He is one of my friends.
He is one of my friend.
He is a one of my friend.
questions.m: He is one of my friends.
a: He is one of my friends.
questions.tip: 'One of' is always followed by a plural noun.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Got people waiting outside.*
questions.tip: 'There is' or 'there are' introduces existence.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *I want to borrow you my book.*
options: I want to lend you my book.
I want to borrow you my book.
I want to borrow my book to you.
I want you to lend my book.
questions.m: I want to lend you my book.
a: I want to lend you my book.
questions.tip: You lend something TO somebody; you borrow something FROM somebody.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Can I follow you to the shop?*
options: May I come with you to the shop?
Can I follow you to the shop?
Can I follow with you to the shop?
May I following you to the shop?
questions.m: May I come with you to the shop?
a: May I come with you to the shop?
questions.tip: 'Follow' means to go behind; going together is 'come with'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *The teacher scold me just now.*
options: The teacher scolded me a moment ago.
The teacher scold me just now.
The teacher just now scolded me.
The teacher was scold me just now.
questions.m: The teacher scolded me a moment ago.
a: The teacher scolded me a moment ago.
questions.tip: The verb needs the past tense: 'scolded'. ('Just now' for a moment ago is acceptable; what is non-standard is using it for any earlier time.)

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Return me my pen.*
options: Please return my pen to me.
Please return me back my pen.
questions.m: Please return my pen to me.
a: Please return my pen to me.
questions.tip: 'Return' takes 'to', and 'return back' is repetitive.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Every of the pupils got a prize.*
options: Every of the pupils got a prize.
Everyone of the pupils got a prize.
Every of the pupil received a prize.
questions.tip: 'Every' goes directly before a singular noun.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *I am having a headache.*
questions.tip: 'Have' meaning 'possess' or 'suffer from' is not used in the continuous form.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Later I call you.*
questions.tip: The future needs 'will'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *This one is mine one.*
questions.tip: The emphatic 'one' at the end is spoken usage only.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *He very the clever.*
questions.tip: 'Very the' is spoken usage; use 'very' alone.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Don't play play.*
questions.tip: State the meaning rather than repeating the verb.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Until now I still don't understand.*
options: Even now I still do not understand.
Until now I still don't understand.
Till now I still don't understand.
Until now I am still not understand.
questions.m: Even now I still do not understand.
a: Even now I still do not understand.
questions.tip: 'Even now' or 'to this day' is the standard form.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Can pass me the salt?*
options: Could you pass me the salt?
Can you pass me the salt or not?
questions.m: Could you pass me the salt?
a: Could you pass me the salt?
questions.tip: A polite request needs a subject.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *My mother she is a nurse.*
options: My mother she is a nurse.
My mother, she is a nurse.
She my mother is a nurse.
questions.tip: Do not repeat the subject with a pronoun.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *I no need help.*
questions.tip: The negative of 'need' is 'do not need'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *She go there by taking bus.*
options: She go there by taking bus.
She goes there by taking bus.
She go there by the bus.
questions.tip: 'By bus' is the set phrase, and the verb needs -s.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Later you fall down, then you know.*
options: Be careful, or you will fall.
Later you fall down, then you know.
Later you will fall down, then you know.
You fall down later, then you know.
questions.m: Be careful, or you will fall.
a: Be careful, or you will fall.
questions.tip: State the warning directly.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Anyhow do also can.*
options: It does not have to be done carefully.
questions.m: It does not have to be done carefully.
a: It does not have to be done carefully.
questions.tip: 'Anyhow' meaning 'carelessly' is spoken usage.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *I am staying at home the whole day already.*
options: I have been at home all day.
I am staying at home the whole day already.
I stay at home whole day already.
I have stayed at home the whole day already.
questions.m: I have been at home all day.
a: I have been at home all day.
questions.tip: A period continuing up to now takes the present perfect.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *The queue damn long.*
questions.tip: Avoid slang intensifiers in written English.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *He is the more better player.*
options: He is the more better player.
He is the most better player.
questions.tip: 'Better' is already a comparative.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Next time onwards I will remember.*
options: Next time onwards I will remember.
From next time onwards I will remember.
Next time onward I will remember.
questions.tip: 'Next time onwards' is not standard; use 'in future' or 'from now on'.

questions.q: Everyday speech: *Discuss about the problem.*
questions.tip: 'Discuss' takes no preposition.

sets.title: Verb pairs that get confused · 40 items
sets.instruction: These pairs look similar but behave differently. Type the correct verb.

questions.q: Please __________ (lend / borrow) me your ruler until recess.
questions.tip: You lend something TO somebody.

questions.q: May I __________ (lend / borrow) your ruler until recess?
questions.tip: You borrow something FROM somebody.

questions.q: My grandmother __________ (taught / learnt) me how to fold dumplings.
questions.tip: A teacher teaches; a pupil learns.

questions.q: I __________ (taught / learnt) how to fold dumplings from my grandmother.
questions.tip: The person receiving the knowledge learns.

questions.q: Please __________ (bring / take) these books to the library for me.
questions.tip: 'Take' means away from where the speaker is.

questions.q: Please __________ (bring / take) me a glass of water from the kitchen.
questions.tip: 'Bring' means towards where the speaker is.

questions.q: The cat likes to __________ (lie / lay) on the warm windowsill.
questions.tip: 'Lie' means to rest; it takes no object.

questions.q: Please __________ (lie / lay) the tray on the table.
questions.tip: 'Lay' means to put something down; it takes an object.

questions.q: The sun __________ (rises / raises) at about seven o'clock here.
questions.tip: 'Rise' means to go up by itself.

questions.q: The shopkeeper __________ (rose / raised) his prices again last month.
questions.tip: 'Raise' means to lift something else.

questions.q: I could not __________ (hear / listen) what he was saying over the noise.
questions.tip: 'Hear' is what reaches your ears; 'listen' is paying attention.

questions.q: Please __________ (hear / listen) carefully to the announcement.
questions.tip: 'Listen' takes 'to' and means to pay attention.

questions.q: Did you __________ (see / watch) the man in the blue shirt?
questions.tip: 'See' is noticing with your eyes.

questions.q: We sat and __________ (watched / saw) the whole match on television last night.
questions.tip: 'Watch' means to follow something over time; 'see' is a single act of noticing.

questions.q: The dog followed him home and would not __________ (leave / go).
questions.tip: 'Leave' means to depart from a place or person.

questions.q: Mrs Tan asked him to __________ (check / control) his answer again.
questions.tip: 'Check' means to look over; 'control' means to direct.

questions.q: The noise from upstairs __________ (disturbed / troubled) my sleep all night.
questions.tip: 'Disturb somebody's sleep' is the set phrase.

questions.q: He __________ (spent / used) all his pocket money on a comic yesterday.
questions.tip: You spend money ON something. 'Spend' is the verb for paying money out.

questions.q: Please __________ (close / near) the door behind you.
questions.tip: 'Close' is the verb; 'near' means nearby.

questions.q: The nurse __________ (took / made) his temperature every two hours.
questions.tip: 'Take a temperature' is the set phrase.

questions.q: Can you __________ (tell / say) the difference between these two shades?
questions.tip: 'Tell the difference' is the set phrase.

questions.q: What did he __________ (say / tell) when you asked him?
questions.tip: 'Say' is followed by the words; 'tell' is followed by a person.

questions.q: He __________ (said / told) me that the shop had closed.
questions.tip: 'Tell' takes a person as its object.

questions.q: I __________ (left / forgot) my wallet on the bus this morning.
questions.tip: You leave an object somewhere; you forget a fact.

questions.q: I __________ (left / forgot) her birthday completely.
questions.tip: You forget information, not an object in a place.

questions.q: She __________ (took / made) a photograph of the whole class.
questions.tip: 'Take a photograph' is the set phrase.

questions.q: They are going to __________ (make / do) a decision this evening.
questions.tip: 'Make a decision' is the set phrase.

questions.q: We must __________ (do / make) our homework before dinner.
questions.tip: 'Do homework' is the set phrase.

questions.q: The heavy rain __________ (caused / made) the match to be cancelled.
questions.tip: 'Caused something to happen' is the correct pattern.

questions.q: He __________ (made / caused) his sister cry by hiding her book.
questions.tip: 'Make somebody do something' takes no 'to'.

questions.q: Please __________ (turn off / close) the tap; you are wasting water.
questions.tip: Taps and lights are turned off, not closed.

questions.q: The shop __________ (opens / opened) at nine every morning.
questions.tip: A daily habit takes the present tense.

questions.q: Her explanation did not __________ (answer / reply) my question.
questions.tip: 'Answer' takes a direct object; 'reply' takes 'to'.

questions.q: She did not __________ (reply / answer) to my message for two days.
questions.tip: 'Reply' is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: He __________ (kicked / knocked) the ball hard with his right foot and it hit the fence.
questions.tip: A ball struck with the foot is kicked.

questions.q: The cold weather __________ (forced / made) him to wear two jumpers.
questions.tip: 'Force somebody to do something' takes 'to'.

questions.q: I must __________ (ask / question) my parents before I agree.
questions.tip: 'Ask' means to request; 'question' suggests doubting them.

questions.q: Please do not __________ (touch / feel) the wet paint.
questions.tip: 'Touch' is the action; 'feel' is the sensation.

questions.q: The doctor told him to __________ (eat / take) more vegetables.
questions.tip: Food is eaten; medicine is taken.

questions.q: Remember to __________ (take / eat) your medicine after dinner.
questions.tip: Medicine is taken, not eaten.

sets.title: Present perfect or past simple · 35 items
sets.instruction: Use the past simple for a finished time, and the present perfect when the time is not finished or not stated. Type the correct form.

questions.q: I __________ (finished / have finished) my homework already.
questions.tip: 'Already' with no stated time takes the present perfect.

questions.q: I __________ (finished / have finished) my homework at six o'clock.
questions.tip: 'At six o'clock' is a finished time.

questions.q: She __________ (lived / has lived) in Singapore since 2019.
questions.tip: 'Since' means the situation continues, so use the present perfect.

questions.q: She __________ (lived / has lived) in Penang for two years before she moved.
questions.tip: The period is over, so use the past simple.

questions.q: __________ (Did / Have) you ever eaten durian?
questions.tip: 'Ever' in a question about any time takes the present perfect.

questions.q: __________ (Did / Have) you eat durian at the party last night?
questions.tip: 'Last night' is a finished time.

questions.q: We __________ (visited / have visited) the museum three times this year.
questions.tip: 'This year' is not over yet.

questions.q: We __________ (visited / have visited) the museum three times last year.
questions.tip: 'Last year' is over.

questions.q: He __________ (lost / has lost) his keys and has not found them yet.
questions.tip: 'Not yet' means the search is still going on, so use the present perfect.

questions.q: He __________ (lost / has lost) his keys on Tuesday but found them again.
questions.tip: A finished event with a stated day.

questions.q: They __________ (just left / have just left) the building.
questions.tip: 'Just' for something a moment ago takes the present perfect.

questions.q: The bus __________ (left / has left) ten minutes ago.
questions.tip: 'Ago' always takes the past simple.

questions.q: I __________ (was / have) never been to Japan.
questions.tip: 'Never been' is present perfect.

questions.q: My father __________ (went / has gone) to Japan in 2015.
questions.tip: A stated year takes the past simple.

questions.q: How long __________ (did / have) you known Priya?
questions.tip: 'How long' about something still true takes the present perfect.

questions.q: When __________ (did / have) you meet Priya?
questions.tip: 'When' asks for a finished point in time.

questions.q: The rain __________ (has / did) stopped, so we can go out.
questions.tip: The result matters now.

questions.q: It __________ (rained / has rained) heavily all last week.
questions.tip: 'Last week' is finished.

questions.q: I __________ (saw / have seen) this film twice and I still like it.
questions.tip: No time is stated and the liking continues.

questions.q: I __________ (saw / have seen) that film on Saturday.
questions.tip: 'On Saturday' is a finished time.

questions.q: She __________ (broke / has broken) her leg and is still in plaster.
questions.tip: 'Is still in plaster' shows the result continues, so use the present perfect.

questions.q: She __________ (broke / has broken) her leg when she was nine.
questions.tip: 'When she was nine' is finished.

questions.q: We __________ (lived / have lived) in this flat since I was born.
questions.tip: 'Since' takes the present perfect.

questions.q: __________ (Did / Has) the postman come yet?
questions.tip: 'Yet' takes the present perfect.

questions.q: The postman __________ (came / has come) at eleven this morning.
questions.tip: A stated clock time that has passed.

questions.q: Nobody __________ (found / has found) the answer so far.
questions.tip: 'So far' means up to now.

questions.q: Nobody __________ (found / has found) the answer in yesterday's lesson.
questions.tip: 'Yesterday' is finished.

questions.q: I __________ (did not see / have not seen) him since Monday.
questions.tip: 'Since Monday' continues to now.

questions.q: I __________ (saw / have seen) him on Monday.
questions.tip: A finished day.

questions.q: Our team __________ (won / has won) every match this season.
questions.tip: The season is still going on.

questions.q: Our team __________ (won / has won) every match last season.
questions.tip: 'Last season' is over.

questions.q: __________ (Did / Have) you finished your lunch?
questions.tip: A question about right now.

questions.q: Prices __________ (rose / have risen) a great deal since last year.
questions.tip: 'Since' takes the present perfect.

questions.q: Prices __________ (rose / have risen) sharply in 2020.
questions.tip: A stated year.

questions.q: This is the first time I __________ (tried / have tried) sushi.
questions.tip: 'This is the first time' is always followed by the present perfect.
